QUESTION:
I paid £4 for an inter-library loan but the other library couldn't supply the book. Do I get my £4 back?

CANDIDATE A:
Yes. It is refunded if the item can't be supplied.

CANDIDATE B:
No. The fee is non-refundable even if the item cannot be supplied.

RESPONSE:
Here are the answers, checked against the policy itself. My earlier notes were wrong on questions 2 and 3 and incomplete on question 4, so the corrections are flagged below.

**1. How long can I borrow a DVD for?**
**1 week** (section 3). You can renew a DVD **once only**, unless another member has reserved it (section 4). Adult cards can have no more than 4 DVDs out at a time.

**2. Picture books on your adult card, returned 5 days late. Will you be charged?**
**Yes.** Section 5 bases overdue charges on the **card used**, not the type of item, and says children's books borrowed on an adult card are charged at the adult rate. *(My notes wrongly said children's books are never charged.)*
- 4 items × 25p × 5 days = **£5.00**. This is well under the £6-per-item cap.
- If you're **65 or over**, you pay half: **£2.50**.
- Borrowing them on your daughter's children's card would have avoided the charge, since children's cards have no overdue charges.

**3. Do you get your £4 inter-library loan fee back?**
**No.** Section 8 says the £4 fee is **non-refundable**, "including where... the lending library cannot supply it." *(My notes wrongly said it would be refunded.)* If you think the library made an error, you could ask about a waiver under section 10, but the policy gives no automatic refund.

**4. Can your branch manager waive the whole £14 after a bereavement?**
**No, not on their own.** Under section 10, a Branch Manager can waive charges of **up to £10** for hardship, bereavement or library error. Requests to waive **more than £10** must go to the **Library Services Manager**, whose decision is final. *(My notes left out this limit.)* Ask your branch manager to refer the full £14 to the Library Services Manager.

Note that at £14 your account is currently **blocked from borrowing** (section 9) until the balance drops below £10.
